prompt: Stage 4-1. You just levelled to 7 and sit at 52 gold, 66 HP, 1-loss streak. Your planned level-8 rolldown is next round, after the 4-2 augment. You are tempted to roll twice now to look at two more shops. What do those two rolls really cost, and is it worth it?

options.label: 4 gold. Two rolls at 2 each; interest is unaffected because you stay above 40
About 5 gold: 4 for the rolls plus 1 interest at 4-2 for dropping under 50, spent on two shops at 10% 4-cost odds when the same 5 gold buys nearly three shops at 30% next round. Not worth it
9 gold: 4 for the rolls plus the whole 5-gold interest tick, because any gold under 50 forfeits interest
Nothing extra: a 4-cost found at 7 is the same 4-cost you would find at 8

explanation:
Do the arithmetic once and the habit dies. The rolls are 4 gold. Dropping from 52 to 48 costs 1 interest at 4-2, because interest is 1 per 10 held, not all or nothing: you go from 5 to 4, not from 5 to 0. So the real price is 5 gold, and you enter the rolldown with 57 instead of 62.

Now what the 5 gold buys. Two shops at level 7 are ten slots at 10% four-cost odds: one 4-cost slot on average, of any 4-cost. The same 5 gold at level 8 next round is two and a half shops, twelve slots at 30%: nearly four 4-cost slots. Every roll at 7 the round before a level-8 rolldown shows you a third of the 4-costs the same gold shows at 8. That is the real cost: not 5 gold, but 5 gold spent at the worst odds you will have all stage.

The player who says interest is unaffected above 40 has the rule wrong, and the player who says it costs 9 has it wrong the other way. Both roll anyway. Do not.
principle: A roll the round before your rolldown costs 2 gold, a point of interest, and two thirds of its odds.
commonMistake: Rolling 'a couple' at 7 the round before levelling to 8, at a third of the odds you are about to pay for.
hint: Count the interest step you cross, then compare what the same gold shows you at 7 today and at 8 tomorrow.
